domain_guidance.summary: This domain covers core physics concepts, neutron multiplication, reactivity changes, and control rod worth. Operators must understand principles governing nuclear fission, reactor startup, steady-state operation, and power changes within the reactor vessel during operational conditions.

This domain addresses fluid flow, heat transfer, steam tables, and thermodynamic cycles applicable to nuclear power plants. Operators must analyze temperature dynamics, enthalpy changes, phase transitions, and heat exchanger performance to maintain proper thermal limits.

This domain focuses on mechanical and electrical components used in power facilities, such as valves, pumps, motors, instrumentation, and circuit breakers. Operators must understand component construction, operational indications, control logic, and failure modes.

This domain covers integrated plant systems including primary cooling, emergency core cooling, secondary steam supply, and electrical distribution. Operators must know system interlocks, flow paths, automatic actions, and control room indications across operating states.

This domain focuses on normal, abnormal, and emergency operating procedures. Operators must follow step-by-step instructions for power maneuvers, system lineups, alarm response, transient mitigation, and emergency declarations to maintain safety boundaries.

This domain addresses regulatory standards, shift clearance, tagout regulations, work authorization, radiation safety controls, and reporting requirements. Operators must comply with 10 CFR Part 55 rules and facility administrative guidelines during daily operations.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: Arrive early at the designated facility testing site with valid identification. Review required administrative documentation beforehand, follow all proctor instructions, and pace yourself while answering the 75 written examination questions carefully.

faq.answer_text: The NRC Nuclear Power Plant Operator License written examination consists of 75 questions. Candidates must answer these questions covering reactor theory, thermodynamics, components, systems, procedures, and administrative requirements.
faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?

faq.answer_text: Candidates must achieve a passing score of 80% on the written portion of the licensing examination. Scoring is evaluated according to U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission standards established under 10 CFR Part 55.

Specific time limits for administering the 75-question examination are governed by U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission standards and facility schedule guidelines. Candidates should confirm exact session timing with their facility training department prior to test day.

Licenses for nuclear power plant operators in the United States are issued by the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) under federal regulations detailed in Title 10 of the Code of Federal Regulations (10 CFR) Part 55.

methodology.summary: This overview was synthesized from official U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) documentation, including NUREG-1021 and 10 CFR Part 55 standards, to reflect verified licensing requirements.

editorial.overview: The NRC Nuclear Power Plant Operator License exam evaluates individuals seeking authorization to manipulate plant controls at nuclear facilities in the United States. Certified by the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC), the licensing process tests operational competence across 6 domains: reactor theory, thermodynamics, components, nuclear power plant systems, procedures, and administrative requirements. Candidates demonstrate technical knowledge required for safe nuclear power plant operations under federal regulatory guidelines.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Study official U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) standards, including NUREG-1021 and NUREG-1122. Focus preparation on the 6 domain areas by reviewing plant system diagrams, thermodynamic concepts, reactor core physics, and site procedures. Practice answering 75 sample questions to achieve at least an 80% passing score. Coordinate with facility training staff to complete required control manipulations and simulation testing prior to taking the licensing examination.
editorial.who_should_take: Candidates preparing to manipulate reactor controls or direct licensed operations at nuclear power facilities should take this examination. Applicants typically complete facility training programs, medical examinations, and control manipulation requirements under U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) guidelines.

There are two categories of licenses: a reactor operator and a senior reactor operator.' and 'The license is issued after the individual passes both a written exam and an operating test.', with 'One is a written test covering reactor theory, thermodynamics, components, nuclear power plant systems, procedures, and administrative requirements. The operating test includes a plant walk-through and a performance demonstration on the plant's reactor simulator.'
